Per-edge verdicts in the handoff merge session. From the 2026-07-31 Grok handoff, verified against primary sources 2026-08-07. TRIAGE of two org-heavy slices that used organisations as nodes and 'publishes'/'funds'/'ritual' edges — all off-model for this corpus. Salvage: 3 genuine recurrent flagship reports (IMF WEO, IMF Fiscal Monitor, OECD Economic Outlook) and 4 report-to-report dependencies verified verbatim against the Fiscal Monitor Methodological and Statistical Appendix (April 2025) and the OECD Economic Outlook Database Inventory (EO107). Everything else — 6 organisation nodes, 2 meeting nodes, 8 financing line-item pseudo-nodes, 12 unwired report candidates, and all 38 handoff edges — is recorded in _dropped. This large drop rate is the intended outcome of the triage. SWEPT 2026-08-09 as part of the corpus-wide _dropped sweep (Tier 3, first item; see planning/dropped-sweep-scoping_2026-08-08.md). Of the 12 unwired report candidates, one (imf-gfsr) was resolved and minted this session on a clean primary-source citation to imf-weo. Three others (wto-trade-monitoring, imf-article-iv, oecd-economic-surveys) were re-checked directly and remain open — cadence and authorship for the WTO/OECD/UNCTAD joint report are now confirmed (previously inferred from the handoff), but the specific data-source or StatCan-citation quotes needed to mint them were not retrieved this session (robots/403 walls, or fetches that returned only page navigation). The 57 `note` entries (organisation nodes, meeting/summit series, financing line-items, and their off-model edges) were reviewed as a set and found to be deliberate, well-reasoned design exclusions from the original triage, not unexamined leads — none were re-opened. Non-branch file (international-organisation galaxy); no dedicated hand-off, tracked here and in planning/OPEN-THREADS_2026-08-08.md thread 2.1.

reports.title: World Economic Outlook (WEO)
reports.description: The IMF's twice-yearly flagship survey of global macroeconomic prospects, with a country-level database of output, inflation, fiscal and external indicators. Historical data and projections are compiled by IMF country desk officers from information gathered in missions to member countries.
reports.cadence_note: Full editions in April and October, with shorter WEO Updates in January and July.

entries.covers: World Economic Outlook, April 2026: Global Economy in the Shadow of War
World Economic Outlook, October 2026 (full edition, expected around the IMF/World Bank Annual Meetings, Oct 12-18, 2026 in Bangkok)

release_schedule.note: IMF's own WEO landing page states the report is 'usually published twice a year, with updates in between' (full editions in April and October; interim Updates in January and July). The April 2026 full edition was released April 14, 2026 and the July 2026 Update on July 8, 2026 (both already past as of 2026-08-11). No dated release calendar for the October 2026 full edition was found on imf.org as of this research; the projection to October 2026 is based on the twice-yearly pattern and the confirmed Oct 12-18, 2026 Annual Meetings dates in Bangkok, Thailand, where the October WEO is traditionally unveiled.

reports.title: Fiscal Monitor
reports.description: One of the IMF's flagship trilogy, surveying public finance developments and projecting fiscal balances and government debt across the membership. Fiscal data follow GFSM 2014 (or SNA 2008 / ESA 2010 based national methodologies) and country projections are drawn from the WEO database.
reports.cadence_note: Published twice yearly alongside the WEO, in April and October.

release_schedule.note: IMF's own Fiscal Monitor landing page states the report is 'prepared twice a year' but does not give explicit months. Confirmed by recent editions: April 2026 edition published 2026-04-15 (imf.org/-/media/files/publications/fiscal-monitor/2026/april/english/text.pdf), October 2025 edition tied to a press briefing dated 2025-10-15, consistent with the on-file cadence_note (April/October, alongside WEO and Spring/Annual Meetings). The 2026 Annual Meetings run 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-18 in Bangkok, so the October 2026 Fiscal Monitor is expected within that window, but the IMF has not yet posted an exact release date, hence month-level precision.

reports.title: OECD Economic Outlook
reports.description: The OECD's twice-yearly analysis of major global economic trends and prospects for the next two years, with projections for output, employment, prices, fiscal and current balances. The underlying database draws historical data from national statistical agencies and OECD statistical databases, on SNA 2008 / ESA 2010 and BPM6 concepts.
reports.cadence_note: Two full editions per year (roughly June and November/December), plus Interim Economic Outlook updates.

entries.covers: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2026 Issue 2 (full twice-yearly edition)
OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2027 Issue 1 (full twice-yearly edition)

release_schedule.note: The OECD publications landing page (oecd.org) and OECD-iLibrary render dynamically via JS and did not expose a dated release calendar to fetch tools. Confirmed via news coverage of actual editions: full twice-yearly editions were released 2025-12-02 (OECD raises UK growth forecast for 2026 on budget impact) and 2026-06-03 (OECD cuts global growth outlook...), consistent with the existing cadence_note (~June and ~November/December). Separately, Interim Economic Outlook updates were observed on 2025-09-23 and 2026-03-26, confirming the interim cadence too, but those are not counted toward this report's releases_per_year=2. Next full edition is therefore projected for early December 2026 based on this observed pattern; no official calendar with an exact day was found.

reports.title: Global Financial Stability Report (GFSR)
reports.description: The third of the IMF's flagship trilogy alongside the World Economic Outlook and the Fiscal Monitor, assessing risks to global financial stability. Minted 2026-08-09 (sweep session, Tier-3 item, grok-h1-international-reports.json) closing a `no-document` lead that had correctly identified this as a genuine recurrent flagship but lacked a verified report-to-report dependency at the time it was triaged.
reports.cadence_note: Published twice yearly alongside the WEO and Fiscal Monitor, in April and October — confirmed by the October 2025 edition's own cross-references to 'the April 2025 Global Financial Stability Report'.

release_schedule.note: No published GFSR release calendar exists. The report is released twice yearly (April and October) timed to the IMF/World Bank Spring and Annual Meetings, alongside the WEO and Fiscal Monitor. Confirmed: April 2026 GFSR was published with a press briefing on April 15, 2026 (transcript: imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/04/15/tr-04142026-press-briefing-transcript-global-financial-stability-report-spring-meetings-2026), and October 2025 GFSR was published October 14, 2025. The 2026 Annual Meetings are confirmed for October 12-18, 2026 in Bangkok, Thailand (imf.org/en/news/seminars/campaigns/2026/10/thailand-2026), so the October 2026 GFSR is expected during that week, most likely mid-week (Tue Oct 13, by analogy with the Oct 14, 2025 Tuesday release and the Apr 14-15, 2026 release), but no exact date has been officially announced yet as of 2026-08-11.

dependencies.basis: Fiscal Monitor Methodological and Statistical Appendix (April 2025): 'Country-specific data and projections for key fiscal variables are based on the April 2025 World Economic Outlook database, unless indicated otherwise, and compiled by IMF staff.'

Fiscal Monitor Methodological and Statistical Appendix (April 2025): 'In many economies, fiscal data follow the IMF's Government Finance Statistics Manual 2014'; also 'In most advanced economies, and in some large emerging market and middle-income economies, fiscal data follow the GFSM 2014'.

OECD Economic Outlook Database Inventory (EO107): 'All OECD countries have implemented the SNA 2008 methodology (or ESA 2010, its European equivalent)', with historical data sourced from 'publications of national statistical agencies and OECD statistical databases such as the OECD Quarterly National Accounts, OECD Annual National Accounts'.

OECD Economic Outlook Database Inventory (EO107): 'All countries follow the BPM6 methodology; BPM6 is the acronym for the sixth edition of the "Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual".'
dependencies.evidence_quote: Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual

dependencies.basis: The October 2025 GFSR's own Preface: 'The report draws out the financial ramifications of economic issues highlighted in the IMF's World Economic Outlook.' Chapter 1 also cross-references a specific WEO forecast directly: 'the mode... of the latest estimate of growth forecast density accords with the IMF's October 2025 World Economic Outlook database forecast for 2026.' `methodology_depends_on` rather than `uses_data_from`, since the Preface frames the relationship as GFSR's own analysis extending WEO's economic narrative, not GFSR reading WEO's numbers as a direct input the way the Fiscal Monitor does.
